newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria clearing system drops individual shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria clearing system drops individual shareholders.

text.p: The Nigerian stock exchange's central securities and clearing system, due to go into operation next month, is dropping individual shareholders to accommodate interested stockbroking firms, the stock exchange's deputy director Ndi Okereke-Onyuike said on Monday.
Some individual shareholders took up shares in the project in 1994 when it could not get assistance from the government or other parties, said Okereke-Onyuike.
She told traders that parties who were initially reluctant to participate in the project now wanted to come on board and so the exchange was compelled to drop the individual shareholders.
"We are asking individual shareholders to drop off because we do not want to be misunderstood," Okereke-Onyuike said. "We want it to be as transparent as possible."
She said brokerages that had not joined before could now take between 100,000 and 500,000 shares at the price of three naira each.

The NSE floated the central securities and clearing system (CSCS) to run the system alongside other shareholders including 39 stockbroking houses, a foreign investor, four local banks and the exchange itself.
Okereke-Onyuike said the exchange went to individuals when it could not get funds from the Nigerian government which thought the stockbrokers should finance the project without any help.
"But now that it is a reality, everybody wants to participate," she said.
The CSCS is expected to revolutionise Nigerian stock dealing when it moves to a computerised settlement and custodian system, cutting transaction costs and time.
It also plans to automate trading before the end of the year, moving away from the current call over system.
"We just want to fully digest the central securities clearing system before automating trading," Hayford Alile, the bourse's director general said in January.
The clearing system which is at least two years late was completed with a grant from the UN Development Programme (UNDP).

Experts from a Canadian firm late last year completed installing the software for the system and various operators have been trained to use it, exchange officials said. It is modelled after that of the Alberta stock exchange in Canada.
